warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 48 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 30 at 11:36AM MDT until September 30 at 2:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar in...
East Central Custer County in southeastern Colorado...
West Central Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 230 PM MDT.

* At 1136 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Up to 1 inch of
rain has fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.75 inches in 1
hour. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in
debris flow moving through the Middle Creek, Squirrel Creek and
Upper Saint Charles. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Middle Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beulah and San Isabel.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake, Northcreek Road county line to Red Mountain Camp
and Northcreek Road from Red Mountain Camp to Beulah.
properties.instruction:
This is a life-threatening situation for in and around the middle
Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Move away and to higher ground immediately.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, roads and normally dry arroyos is likely. The heavy rains
will likely trigger rockslides, mudslides and debris flows in steep
terrain, especially in and around these areas.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 2:30 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 2:30 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 30 at 11:27AM MST until October 1 at 12:30AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1230 AM MST /130 AM MDT/ Tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.
Further rises in the water levels are expected. Deadly flooding
over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1111 AM MST /1211 PM MDT/, river gauges along the Little
Colorado River reported rises upstream of Holbrook and Winslow
this morning. Flooding has now been observed at Holbrook.
Additional flooding expected downstream towards Winslow, and Bird
Springs later this afternoon and evening.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Little Colorado River.

Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Winslow, Holbrook, Bird Springs, Hibbard, Manila, Joseph City,
Sunrise, Leupp, and Jackrabbit.

- For Little Colorado at Joseph City:
At 10:30am MST /11:30am MDT/ the stage was 5.93 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 6.53 feet is expected at 1:00pm MST /2:00pm
MDT/ Wednesday.
Impacts:
At 7.5 feet: Potential downstream lowland overflow.

- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 11:00am MST /12:00pm MDT/ the stage was 18.09 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 19.18 feet is expected at 5:00pm MST /6:00pm
MDT/ Wednesday.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp will be
within 3 feet of flooding problems. Minor lowland overflow on
right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
At 19.0 feet: Overflow on right bank. Water approaches Ames Acres
and Bushman Acres on left bank in Winslow area. Erosion is likely
on the levee on the left bank. Downstream, the approaches to the
bridge over the river on route 71 near Bird Springs will flood
and evacuations of homes near the intersection of route 2 and
route 71 are conducted.

- For Little Colorado at Little Colorado River at Holbrook:
At 10:30am MST /11:30am MDT/ the stage was 15.77 feet.
Flood Stage is 15.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 16.24 feet is expected at 12:00pm MST
/1:00pm MDT/ Wednesday.
Impacts:
At 15.5 feet: Railroad bridge affected. Overflow on South Bank.
- This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Homolovi State Park, Hunt Park, McHood Park, Standin on the
Corner Park, Sacred Heart Park and Winslow City Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Clear Creek Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.
